summary: Sweden is permissive for the roof rat, now confirmed in writing by the Swedish Board of Agriculture (Jordbruksverket, June 2026). There is no species-specific ban: R. rattus is not on the EU invasive-species Union list (Reg. 1143/2014) and not on Sweden's national invasive list (Förordning 2026:311). The Animal Welfare Act (Djurskyddslagen 2018:1192) regulates HOW animals are kept, not WHICH rodent species, and the Board of Agriculture's rules (SJVFS 2019:15) cover rats generically as gnagare. Jordbruksverket confirmed it is permitted to keep R. rattus as pets as long as they are not wild-caught, with NO permit and NO registration; only PROFESSIONAL (yrkesmässig) keeping/breeding/selling needs to check with the county board (länsstyrelsen), larger-scale but non-professional hobby activity is EXEMPT from the permit requirement (except breeding animals intended as feeder/feed animals). Welfare and enclosure standards apply (SJVFS 2019:15 ch. 1; enclosure size/enrichment per SJVFS 2019:29 ch. 11 §§17-18). Ironically R. rattus is classed as EXTINCT (RE) in the wild in Sweden, so captive pets pose essentially zero invasion risk. Cross-border transport of pet rodents needs no registration (commercial transport requires authorisation as an animal transporter); intra-EU commercial movement, or more than 5 pet animals, needs an Article 151 Animal Health Law self-declaration from a registered establishment, no TRACES notification and no health certificate. Non-EU import is tighter.
agency_confirmations: Swedish Board of Agriculture (Jordbruksverket), written reply June 2026: it is permitted to keep Rattus rattus as pets in Sweden as long as the animals are not caught in the wild, with NO permit and NO registration required (SJVFS 2019:15, ch. 1 §§4-5). Welfare and enclosure-size/enrichment standards apply (SJVFS 2019:15 ch. 1; SJVFS 2019:29 ch. 11 §§17-18). A permit is only relevant for PROFESSIONAL (yrkesmässig) keeping, breeding, or selling, larger-scale but non-professional hobby activity is exempt (except breeding animals intended as feeder/feed animals); professional operators should ask their county administrative board (länsstyrelsen) whether a permit is needed. Cross-border transport of pet rodents needs no registration; commercial transport requires authorisation as an animal transporter, and intra-EU commercial movement (or more than 5 pet animals) needs an Article 151 Animal Health Law self-declaration from a registered establishment, no TRACES notification and no health certificate. The agency also confirmed the '6 enclosures' figure refers to the number of cages.

keep.why: Jordbruksverket confirmed (June 2026) it is permitted to keep R. rattus as pets as long as they are not wild-caught, with no permit and no registration (SJVFS 2019:15 ch. 1 §§4-5). Djurskyddslagen 2018:1192 imposes welfare duties but no species ban; R. rattus is absent from the EU Union list and Sweden's national invasive list (Förordning 2026:311). Keepers must meet welfare/enclosure standards (SJVFS 2019:15 ch. 1; enclosure size/furnishing/enrichment per SJVFS 2019:29 ch. 11 §§17-18) and the social-species rule (keep ≥2 rats).
keep.governing_law: Djurskyddslag 2018:1192; SJVFS 2019:15 ch. 1 §§4-6; SJVFS 2019:29 ch. 11 §§17-18; Förordning 2026:311 (R. rattus not listed); Reg. (EU) 1143/2014 (not listed).

breed.why: Jordbruksverket confirmed (June 2026) that keeping, breeding, or selling pets other than dogs and cats at larger scale but NOT in a professional manner is EXEMPT from the permit requirement, so a private/hobby rattery needs no permit regardless of cage count. Only PROFESSIONAL (yrkesmässig) breeding must ask the county administrative board (länsstyrelsen) whether a permit is required, and the exemption does NOT cover breeding animals intended to be sold as feeder/feed animals. (The agency clarified the '6 enclosures' figure refers to the number of cages.) Welfare standards apply throughout.
breed.governing_law: Djurskyddslag 2018:1192 6 kap.; Djurskyddsförordning 2019:66; SJVFS 2019:15; SJVFS 2019:27 (permit obligation, professional activity).

sell_give.why: Free transfers and sales between hobbyists are permit-free: Jordbruksverket confirmed (June 2026) that larger-scale but non-professional keeping/breeding/selling of pets other than dogs and cats is exempt from the permit requirement (Sweden has no separate pet-shop licence). Only PROFESSIONAL (yrkesmässig) selling must check with the county administrative board (länsstyrelsen). SJVFS 2019:15 sets sale conditions (health checks, documentation). No species ban or price cap on captive-bred R. rattus; the exemption excludes breeding animals sold as feeder/feed animals.
sell_give.governing_law: Djurskyddslag 2018:1192 6 kap.; SJVFS 2019:15; SJVFS 2019:27 (permit only for professional activity).

transport.why: Jordbruksverket confirmed (June 2026): cross-border transport of pet rodents needs NO registration. If animals are moved in connection with an economic activity, the carrier must be authorised as an animal transporter (SJVFS 2019:7; minimum rodent-container requirements in Annex/Bilaga 1.11). For intra-EU COMMERCIAL movement, or movement of more than 5 pet animals, no health certificate and no TRACES notification are required, but an Article 151 Animal Health Law (Reg. 2016/429) self-declaration is, issued by the operator at the place of origin, which must itself be registered as an establishment for terrestrial animals (Art. 84). There is no numeric cap on a single commercial movement and no fixed template for the self-declaration. Non-EU import follows different, tighter rules. Internal transport is unregulated beyond welfare. Never release.
transport.governing_law: SJVFS 2019:7 (transport of live animals; Bilaga 1.11 rodent containers); EU Reg. 2016/429 (Animal Health Law, Arts. 84 & 151); Djurskyddslag 2018:1192.

restrictions.summary: Only PROFESSIONAL (yrkesmässig) keeping, breeding, or selling of pet rodents needs to check with your county administrative board (länsstyrelsen) about a permit, larger-scale but non-professional hobby activity is EXEMPT (Jordbruksverket, June 2026), except breeding animals intended to be sold as feeder/feed animals, which is not exempt. Transport in connection with an economic activity requires authorisation as an animal transporter (SJVFS 2019:7). Meet the welfare rules (minimum enclosure size, enrichment, and keep rats in groups of ≥2). Never release a roof rat.
steps: If operating professionally, ask your länsstyrelsen whether a permit is required
For transport in connection with an economic activity, register as an authorised animal transporter with Jordbruksverket
restrictions.where_to_file: Länsstyrelsen (county administrative board); Jordbruksverket for transporter authorisation

inquiry_focus: (1) Does SJVFS 2019:27 set the '6 enclosures' figure as the threshold at which rodent keeping/breeding becomes 'larger scale' requiring a 6 kap. Djurskyddslagen permit, and does 'enclosure' mean a distinct cage or a breeding colony? (2) For importing more than 5 captive-bred R. rattus from another EU member state, is a health certificate / TRACES notification required, or does the 5-animal personal exemption not apply to commercial transfers? (3) Does the county permit process distinguish Rattus rattus from R. norvegicus in any way given R. rattus's extinct-in-the-wild (RE) status in Sweden?
